evidence.observation: The core apply primitive. It counts occurrences of search_text in original_text (num = original_text.count(search_text)) and, with the guard restored, raises SearchTextNotUnique when num > 1 before ever calling original_text.replace. Returning None when num == 0 makes an absent search a clean refusal. Because the raise happens before the replacement, a non-unique block produces no output at all, so no occurrence can be partially mutated. For a block that occurs exactly once it returns the text with exactly one substitution, leaving whitespace-identical sibling blocks untouched.

Typed ValueError subclass that is the contract's failure signal for a non-unique search block. It is raised by search_and_replace (line 439) and caught by callers, which is how 'fails without partial mutation' is expressed: the exception unwinds before any buffer is rewritten.

Strategy driver: iterates the (strategy, preprocs) pairs and returns the first truthy result via try_strategy. It does not swallow SearchTextNotUnique, so a non-unique exact search raises out of the whole flexible pipeline instead of falling through to a lossier strategy that would apply the wrong edit. This is the entry point exercised by the fixture at the same shape as udiff_coder.flexi_just_search_and_replace ([(search_and_replace, all_preprocs)]).

Runs one strategy under one preproc combination (strip_blank_lines / relative_indent / reverse_lines). The non-unique fixture hits this with the first preproc (False, False, False), so the uniqueness check sees the raw newline/whitespace text and raises before any preprocessing could blur the count. Returning falsy (None) for misses and letting SearchTextNotUnique propagate is what makes the refusal atomic.

The preproc combinations paired with search_and_replace by both editblock_strategies (line 547) and udiff_strategies (line 558); the first entry (False, False, False) is the literal, whitespace-exact interpretation. It anchors the fixture's use of find/replace as the exact-edit path before any flexible newline/whitespace normalization.

Caller-side contract: it invokes flexi_just_search_and_replace inside a try/except SearchTextNotUnique and maps the exception to new_content = None (lines 274-277). A None result makes do_replace/apply_hunk skip writing the file, which is the concrete 'no partial mutation' behavior the fixture models. It also short-circuits repeated tiny-context hunks (content.count(before) > 1) at line 271.

claims.claim: An exact newline/whitespace-distinct edit succeeds exactly once: when search_text occurs once in original_text, search_and_replace substitutes it a single time, the byte-identical sibling block is unchanged, and the input buffer is not mutated in place.

A non-unique edit fails without partial mutation: when search_text occurs more than once, search_and_replace raises SearchTextNotUnique from the num > 1 guard at line 438-439 before original_text.replace is reached, so the caller observes None and the buffer stays byte-identical to its input rather than being rewritten at every occurrence.

The dependency-free minimal source change was to restore the uniqueness guard in search_and_replace that the fixture baseline had commented out; the SearchTextNotUnique class at line 524 and the except handler at udiff_coder.py:276 were otherwise unreachable, and re-running the non-unique scenario without the guard silently applies 2 substitutions (over-application) instead of refusing.

flexible_search_and_replace and try_strategy propagate the typed SearchTextNotUnique error instead of falling through to a lossier strategy, and the caller directly_apply_hunk maps that error to a None result, which is the mechanism that turns a non-unique edit into an atomic, no-mutation refusal.

conclusion: The contract for the distinct newline/whitespace edit fixture holds. search_and_replace now rejects a non-unique search block by raising SearchTextNotUnique before any replacement, so the operation is atomic: an exact (unique) block is applied exactly once while a block occurring twice fails with the original buffer returned unchanged. The executable fixture .prale-eval/contract_fixture.py drives the real production functions over the alpha/beta newline-and-indent fixture and all 10 checks pass (exit 0); a counterfactual re-run with the guard disabled shows the over-application (2 substitutions) that the contract forbids. The only source change is the restored 2-line uniqueness guard in aider/coders/search_replace.py; no task metadata, oracle files, locks, or git config were modified.
